recognize_zh: 低倍（10x）CSF 細胞離心抹片中細胞極度密集，幾乎全是單一形態、深藍色細胞質的圓形細胞，僅夾雜少量紅血球；正常 CSF 細胞應極少，這種單調細胞大量浸潤提示腫瘤侵犯，但低倍下無法判定細胞種類，需搭配高倍與流式確認為漿細胞。
features: Low-power cytospin with marked hypercellularity, far exceeding normal CSF cellularity
Monotonous population of round, discohesive cells with deeply basophilic (blue) cytoplasm and dark nuclei
Cells arranged in crowded sheets and aggregates due to cytocentrifugation
Few scattered red cells and occasional larger cells; background proteinaceous material
Plasma cell features (eccentric nucleus, hof) cannot be resolved at this magnification
describe_en: Low-power examination of the CSF cytospin shows striking hypercellularity composed of a monotonous population of round, discohesive cells with deeply basophilic cytoplasm, accompanied by a few red blood cells. Cytologic detail is limited at this magnification, and definitive lineage assignment requires high-power review and ancillary studies. In the context of known plasma cell myeloma, with plasma cells confirmed on high-power examination and flow cytometry, the findings are consistent with extensive leptomeningeal involvement by myeloma.

ddx.vs: At low power these look identical; high-power morphology (no hof, blast chromatin) and flow cytometry (CD19/CD20 or CD34/TdT rather than CD38/CD138 with cytoplasmic light chain) separate them.
Reactive CSF shows a mixed population of small lymphocytes, monocytes and occasional plasma cells with polytypic markers rather than a monomorphic basophilic infiltrate.
Traumatic tap produces numerous red cells with a blood-like leukocyte mix, whereas red cells here are sparse relative to the dense monotonous infiltrate.
